body.statement:
There exist constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on the declared model constants, such that for every deterministic threshold sequence and all sufficiently large \(n\),
\[
 c r_n\leq R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star
 \leq\sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}|\widehat\theta_n-\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})|
 \leq C r_n.
\]
Moreover,
\[
 \inf_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}
 \{\psi_{\delta_n}(P^{\mathrm F})\in\mathrm{CI}_n\}\geq1-\alpha,
 \qquad
 \sup_{P^{\mathrm F}\in\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}}
 \mathbb E_{(P^{\mathrm F})^{\otimes n}}[\operatorname{len}(\mathrm{CI}_n)]\leq Cr_n,
\]
and every uniformly \((1-\alpha)\)-honest observed-sample interval over \(\mathcal M^{\mathrm F}\) has worst-case expected length at least \(cr_n\).  Thus \(R_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\asymp L_{n,\mathrm F}^\star\asymp r_n\), attained by the same total-Gram estimator and bias-aware interval as in the observed-data experiment.
body.justification: This theorem is the exact causal transport corollary: the purpose-built full-data class maps onto the observed class, the causal bridge aligns the targets, and the observed sampling law is unchanged. The novel minimax-risk and honest expected-length frontier is established by the observed-data theorems; this result transfers it, including attainment, without claiming an independently novel causal frontier.
body.gap: Published threshold-policy identification does not supply this paper's explicit onto full-data lift or the deterministic triangular-array observed frontier. The theorem closes only the transport step for the declared structural class, using the proved pointwise bridge under fiberwise structural-mean continuity and the observed-margin surjection.
body.consumer: The theorem transports the observed frontier to the same exact lower-threshold policy specification accepted by the official \(\texttt{lmtp}\) user-policy workflow and motivates a future implementation of the total-Gram estimator and interval; it does not claim that workflow currently implements them.
